candidates.source_name: Centrálny register zmlúv (CRZ) — daily change-batch export
candidates.why_relevant: The contract-side counterpart to the tender notices: CRZ holds all state contracts since 1 Jan 2011 and publishes daily XML change batches (ZIP) at a predictable URL pattern (http://www.crz.gov.sk/export/YYYY-MM-DD.zip). This is the single best route to the *executed* contract corpus (values, parties, dates) needed for supplier-side / value-side questions about bank and payments vendors.
candidates.access_status: public; documented rate limits (approx. 1 request / 2s daytime 06:00-20:00, <3/s at night)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily incremental pull of the dated ZIP change batch, parse XML into a local contract store; backfill by iterating dates from 2011; strictly respect the published rate limits.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sk-language search on CRZ open data/API; snowball from data.gov.sk CRZ dataset
queries_used: crz.gov.sk otvorené dáta API export zmlúv CSV centrálny register zmlúv

candidates.why_relevant: Civil-society re-publication of the whole Slovak state-register corpus in cleaned, queryable form: CRZ contracts from 2011, register of legal entities (RPO v2), obchodný vestník, accounting records. candidates.legal_status: derived from public registers; check the site's terms for the free vs premium tiers

negative_findings.description: znasichdani.sk — the Aliancia Fair-play / Vizuálny obchodný register project (launched 2011) that let users search which state contracts were won by companies linked to a given person — appears to be defunct. A direct fetch of https://znasichdani.sk/ failed with DNS resolution failure (ENOTFOUND), and secondary sources state the project was terminated in 2018.
negative_findings.result_summary: DNS did not resolve; corroborating reporting says the project ended in 2018. Named in the cell scope but not collectable as a live source. Not recorded as definitively dead on the fetch alone — the DNS failure plus independent reporting together support the conclusion.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This was the cell's designated beneficial-ownership-to-contract linking tool. Its loss means person-to-supplier-to-contract linkage must be rebuilt from RPO/obchodný register joins (e.g. via Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital or FinStat) rather than taken off the shelf. Historical snapshots may still exist in web archives.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated ÚVO open-data API host (e.g. an 'opendata.uvo.gov.sk' style endpoint) was confirmed in this pass. ÚVO bulletin data appears to be published *through* the national catalogue (data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk) rather than via a first-party ÚVO API. A tender for an 'Open API rozhranie pre portál OPENDATA' was itself found as a procurement notice on uvostat.sk, suggesting such an interface was procured at some point.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in sk and en; found catalogue-mediated distributions and third-party APIs, but no verified first-party ÚVO API base URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects pipeline design: the collector should target catalogue distributions and CRZ exports rather than assume a first-party ÚVO REST API. Worth a dedicated follow-up check against uvo.gov.sk itself.

negative_findings.description: uvo.gov.sk returned an 'Error' page in a search result snippet during this pass, and no direct fetch of the main ÚVO site was completed here.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as a hypothesis only — the official portal is almost certainly live and either bot-defended or intermittently unavailable. Not recorded as dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The official portal is the upstream of every source in this cell; its availability pattern determines whether the open-data layer must be the primary collection route.

negative_findings.description: OtvorenéZmluvy.sk current operational status could not be confirmed. Search results describe the portal and its ~300k contracts and a GitHub organisation exists, but no direct fetch was performed and no recent (2024-2026) evidence of active updating was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with low confidence and access_status 'unverified' rather than as live or dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If dormant, its red-flag scoring layer would need to be reimplemented over CRZ rather than consumed; if live, it saves substantial work.

negative_findings.description: No Slovak open-data or civil-society product was found that is specific to banking, payments or financial-sector procurement. All discovered analytics layers are sector-agnostic and must be filtered by CPV code, buyer identity or supplier identity to isolate banking/payments relevance.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched sk and en for procurement-analytics tooling; every hit is a general-purpose corpus or aggregator.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sector isolation is our own work, not something the ecosystem provides. Requires an explicit CPV shortlist (financial/insurance services, banking software, payment terminals, card personalisation, ATM/self-service, IT services) and a curated buyer list (NBS, Slovenská pošta, state banks and agencies) to be defined before collection.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code shortlist for banking and payments has been fixed. uvostat.sk exposes per-CPV pages (e.g. /cpvkod/{id}) and TenderRadar filters by CPV, but the specific CPV branches covering financial services, banking software, payment terminals/POS, ATMs, card issuance and related IT services were not enumerated in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive an explicit CPV shortlist from the EU CPV taxonomy (66xxxxxx financial/insurance, 48xxxxxx software, 30xxxxxx office/computing incl. payment terminals, 72xxxxxx IT services) and validate each against uvostat.sk CPV pages for actual Slovak notice volume.

coverage_gaps.description: The e-procurement execution platforms named by aggregators — EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém, elektronické trhovisko), JOSEPHINE, ERANET — were identified only indirectly, through third-party aggregators. Their own open-data/API surfaces were not investigated in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a follow-up pass to EKS (eks.sk / elektronickatrhovisko), JOSEPHINE and ERANET to determine whether each publishes open data or an API; low-value purchases (where much payments hardware and small IT is bought) live disproportionately on these platforms.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/snapshot strategy was identified for notices that are delisted from the official portal, nor for defunct civil-society mirrors (znasichdani.sk). Web-archive coverage of Slovak procurement sites was not assessed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test Wayback Machine and Common Crawl coverage for uvo.gov.sk, znasichdani.sk and otvorenezmluvy.sk; adopt the OCDS all-time release plus Opentender bulk as the durable historical base layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Joining suppliers across ÚVO notices, CRZ contracts, OCDS records and company registers relies on IČO and on OCDS ocid, but no mapping between the identifier schemes used by uvostat.sk, Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital and the OCDS publication was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and test an identifier crosswalk early (IČO <-> uvostat obstarávateľ/dodávateľ id <-> ocid <-> TED notice id) before any volume collection; the Ekosystém RPO v2 dataset is the natural spine.

coverage_gaps.description: Re-use terms were not read in full for the commercial/semi-commercial analytics layers (uvostat.sk, transparex.sk, transpera.sk, tendermonitor.sk, tenderradar.sk) or for the Slovensko.Digital premium tier.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before any automated collection from these hosts, read robots.txt and terms of use, and prefer licensed API access; restrict free-tier use to manual verification.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal and self-government contract registers outside CRZ (the ~130 smaller registers that OtvorenéZmluvy aggregated, plus commercial register services such as eGovZmluvy/zmluvy.egov.sk) were touched only in passing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map the sub-CRZ registers used by municipalities, schools and regional authorities; relevant because local-government payment/POS and banking-services contracts often never reach CRZ or the ÚVO bulletin.

brief: Slovakia has an unusually deep open-data and analytics layer over public procurement, in three tiers: (1) official machine-readable publication — the national catalogue at data.slovensko.sk (with a DCAT-AP-SK SPARQL endpoint) carrying ÚVO Vestník datasets, the legacy CKAN portal data.gov.sk, and the CRZ contract register with predictable daily XML change-batch exports since 2011; (2) civil-society re-publication — Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital's weekly SQL dumps and rate-limited APIs over CRZ and the company registers, Red Flags for state IT project scoring, Transparency International Slovensko's tooling and methodologies, and Nadácia Zastavme korupciu's quantitative analyses of the post-2024 collapse in competitive tendering; and (3) standardised/international mirrors — the Slovak OCDS publication in the OCP Data Registry, Opentender.eu (GTI/DIGIWHIST, which adds below-threshold national data to TED), plus TED Open Data and the EU Public Procurement Data Space. A commercial analytics tier (uvostat.sk, transparex.sk with its T-index, transpera.sk, tendermonitor.sk, tenderradar.sk) adds supplier/buyer profiling and CPV-level market metrics that the official portals cannot answer, at the cost of paywalls and restrictive terms. The main weaknesses of the cell are that the flagship beneficial-ownership tool znasichdani.sk is defunct (DNS failure plus reporting of a 2018 shutdown), no first-party ÚVO API was confirmed, and nothing in the ecosystem is sector-specific — banking and payments relevance must be carved out ourselves via a CPV shortlist and a curated buyer/supplier list.
